title: Theodore Grunewald as a musician and the value of playing in tune
summary: Asked about Mr. Grunewald, DeDroit describes him as a capable pianist with fine intonation, which he says made his band better than other so-called jazz bands.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Sure, but I want to ask you one question. Yes, we can. What about Mr. Grunwald? Did he play an instrument?

Mr. Grunwald was a very capable piano player, but he would only do it around us, because he was a big man. The Grunwald Music Store was named after Mr. Grunwald. I said to Louis a while ago, if I was a mistake, his name was Theodore, Theodore Grunwald. He was a fine musician and you couldn't fool him. He knew music, and he knew musicians when he heard of him. He was great on intonation, and that's what we had. When we played, we played in tune. That's what made our jazz just a little bit better than the other so-called jazz, because the musicians, they were not schooled. I doubt it sometimes that they didn't tune.
